correctness.rationale: [1], Corollary 36 supplies the quartic polar form. Differentiation gives \(z^2=\gamma t\) and \(t^3+1=2z^3\) for exact triple contact. Affine singular elimination proves smoothness exactly when \(\gamma\ne0\) and \(\gamma^3\ne1\); slopes zero and infinity are separately handled. The compactified cubic is smooth and the \([Z^2:TW]\) morphism is basepoint-free of degree six. Six distinct deck maps give \(\operatorname{Gal}\cong S_3\); direct local parameter analysis gives index two at exactly three points over each of zero and the cube roots of unity, unramified elsewhere. Riemann--Hurwitz checks genus one. The standalone SymPy checker ran and verified critical algebraic identities; it does not purport to independently certify all geometric statements.

originality.rationale: The new statement computes the entire varying flex-incidence curve, its elliptic genus, degree-six Galois cover, full \(S_3\) deck group and four branch fibers. Source [1] proves the existence of six flex lines for each generic Hesse parameter but does not assert or tabulate this cover. Exact polynomial aliases and broader descriptions were searched in primary sources, published web records and the mathematical semantic database. No covering statement was identified. The 1916 Chisini source is a genuine uninspected historical risk; the assessment is not an independence or exhaustive-priority certificate.
residual_risks: Chisini 1916 full text was not available; an implicit equivalent global flex-incidence or monodromy calculation cannot be excluded.

value.rationale: [1] identifies six concurrent flex tangents as the lines governing six Kodaira type-II fibers. Determining the exact connected incidence cover as the Fermat elliptic curve, its full nonabelian permutation monodromy and complete boundary branch profile is a natural global geometric classification of their variation, not an arbitrary finite sample, unmotivated parameter slice, or restatement of the source existence theorem. The result is scoped to marked Hesse coordinates and leaves other flexes and coarse-moduli monodromy outside its claims.
